Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-11
Time: 15:00 - 15:52 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood CSM); Lara Kim, Owen Park, Priya Desai, Samir Qureshi (Harvest)
Links shared: onboarding deck https://rwd.io/harvest-kickoff-deck, security pack https://rwd.io/security-pack, staging invite link (sent after call)

Summary (auto): Kickoff and onboarding sequencing. Primary asks: VPC peering window, SAML integration, pilot success metrics, reserved capacity worksheet.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for hopping on — good to meet you all. quick intros?
[00:12] Lara (Harvest): hi i'm lara, head of ml platform at harvest. we own infra and the rollout plan for the pilot.
[00:18] Owen (Harvest): owen, eng manager; i'll own the network side with samir.
[00:24] Samir (Harvest): samir, s-r-e. i'll look at peering and firewall.
[00:28] Priya D (Harvest): priya desai, security — i'll review compliance stuff, SOC2, KMS and encryption.
[00:33] Maya: great, on our side diego will run the technical bits and priya rao from success will handle the onboarding cadence.
[00:40] Diego (Redwood SE): hey all, excited to dig in. quick note, i'm going to mention dedicated vs hosted and some perf numbers — those are baseline, we'll bench them in staging.

[02:05] Maya: objective for today — align on who does what, confirm pilot success metrics, decide initial capacity mode (hosted to start then dedicated reserved or direct dedicated?) and get dates for network peering and staging access. anything to add?
[02:17] Lara: sounds right. timeline: we want pilot running in production-like staging in three weeks, maybe start traffic in four.
[02:24] Maya: ok three weeks to staging, four to pilot — that's tight but doable. we'll need your firewall window for VPC peering and SSO details.

[05:10] Diego: technical constraints — for latency-sensitive endpoints we recommend Redwood Dedicated if you need sub-80ms p95 for 512 token seqs; otherwise hosted with our burst pool and prefix cache can hit similar economics. small caveat — model quantization and sequence length affect throughput.
[05:38] Owen: can you remind me of the sizing? we have n1-standard on gcp for other services, but for inference we will likely use your managed endpoints.
[05:48] Diego: yeah for Hosted API you don't need gpu infra, we manage it. For Dedicated we size a reserved pool; typical configuration for your expected 300 qps peak text-generation workload would be X GPUs — i'll attach a worksheet.

[08:01] Samir: firewall and peering — do you need fixed IPs? our secops needs static egress allow-lists.
[08:08] Maya: we can provide egress ranges for hosted customers; for Private/VPC and Dedicated we do VPC peering with customer, so we will work with your network team on specific subnets and routes. diego will send a template.

[09:22] Priya D: about data in flight and at rest — how are tokens logged, do you keep raw prompts, and how to integrate our KMS?
[09:31] Diego: good q. by default hosted retains some request metadata for billing and observability but we offer configs to disable retention and enterprise plans include BYOK with KMS/HSM options. our security pack (shared) has details; note some transcriptions may call it "Redwood Dedicate" in older docs — sorry for the typo in the pdf.

[12:50] Owen: latency targets — our SLA internal bar is p95 < 120ms. for generation with 256 tokens, can you meet that on hosted?
[13:03] Diego: hosted for that size usually in the 90-140 p95 range depending on model. For guaranteed lower p95 you'll want dedicated and pin a model variant; also batching behavior can add jitter. We'll run bench with your prompt set and measure.

[16:18] Maya: ok so concrete sequencing: 1) staging tenant and invites 2) VPC peering/ firewall window 3) bench run 4) pilot start. does that map to your internal plan?
[16:29] Lara: yes, that maps. one question: can we do SAML SSO first or after staging?
[16:35] Priya Rao (Redwood CSM): we typically do basic access first (API keys and user invites) then SAML in parallel; SAML can take a week due to idp configuration.

[19:50] Samir: about peering — do you require direct cross-project peering or can we NAT? we prefer peering for stability.
[19:58] Diego: peering is cleaner. we support VPC peering and private link options depending on cloud. i'll include the network runbook.

[22:40] Owen: any gotchas for egress ports or ephemeral ranges? our infra team is strict.
[22:46] Diego: we'll share the IP ranges and port list; also expect TLS 443 on service endpoints and a few control plane ports. sometimes k-v cache references get munged in notes as "k v cash" — ignore that, it's our kv cache for prefix caching.

[26:12] Priya D: about audit logs and compliance — do you produce tenant-level audit logs and can we export to our SIEM?
[26:21] Maya: yes, enterprise plans include audit logs and you can stream to your SIEM via our log forwarder. we'll share the audit schema.

[29:34] Lara: we need to define pilot success metrics. proposing: 1) accuracy/regression threshold on 200 eval prompts 2) cost per 1k tokens under $X 3) <5% error rate and p95 under 150ms.
[29:50] Diego: that looks reasonable. for accuracy we recommend Redwood Optimize suggestions and we'll flag any quality deltas. we'll run a baseline eval and then the pilot.

[33:05] Maya: pricing and reserved capacity — we'll send the reserved capacity worksheet and a recommended ramp schedule. quick note: you mentioned comparing vendors earlier — who else are you evaluating?
[33:18] Lara: mostly Anthropic (safety angle) and some internal experiments on OpenAI endpoints. also evaluating some self-hosted runtimes.
[33:27] Maya: good to know; we'll include comparisons and cost models in the worksheet.

[36:40] Diego: on the bench plan — i'll run two tests: latency-focused (single request p95) and throughput (sustained qps) using your prompt set. we should run at least two window sizes for seq length: 128 and 512 tokens.
[36:53] Samir: that helps. is there a preferred bench script?
[36:57] Diego: i'll share a repo link and a script. also note that our automatic prefix caching can reduce cost for repeated prefixes but it's workload-dependent.

[40:12] Priya D: please include data residency / logs retention options explicitly — we have a customer requirement doc.
[40:20] Maya: yes we'll include retention settings; enterprise/private deployments can keep logs off platform or configured to zero retention.

[44:04] Lara: timeline reminder: staging by 10/18, pilot by 10/25 if staging checks out. any blockers?
[44:14] Maya: blockers: security review feedback, your network peering window, and getting the prompt set.
[44:22] Priya D: we'll try to get the prompt set by 10/13.

[47:00] Owen: one more — do you support canary rollouts and automatic fallback if model hits errors?
[47:08] Diego: yes, Redwood Console supports canary traffic splits, A/B and automatic fallback to a lower-capacity model variant. we'll show this in the staging demo.

[49:55] Maya: ok recap: Maya send runbook & pricing worksheet by 10/13; Diego send bench scripts + network runbook and schedule peering walkthrough for 10/15; Priya Rao provision staging tenant by 10/14; Harvest to share prompts by 10/13 and confirm pilot profile by 10/18.
[50:18] Lara: confirmed. thanks everyone.
[50:25] Priya Rao: i'll follow up with a calendar invite for the network walkthrough and add action items to the onboarding board.
[50:35] Samir: thanks — i'll loop in secops and netops.
[50:40] Maya: thanks all, we'll send notes and links after the call.
[50:48] Owen: bye everyone.

Auto-detected action items (generated): Maya to send runbook & pricing; Diego to share bench + network runbook; Priya Rao to provision staging tenant; Harvest to share pilot prompts.
